sanskrit: bālasya hatabandhoś ca pārtha kiṃ cid ajānataḥ prasādaṃ kuru dharmajña mā manyuvaśam anvagāḥ
english: O Pārtha, show grace to this child, whose kinsmen are slain and who knows little of these matters; O knower of dharma, do not yield to the sway of wrath.

sanskrit: tam anāryaṃ nṛśaṃsaṃ ca vismṛtyāsya pitāmaham āgaskāriṇam atyarthaṃ prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: Forgetting that his grandfather was ignoble, cruel, and a grievous wrongdoer, you ought to grant him your grace.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvatyāṃ karuṇaṃ duḥśalāyāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ saṃsmṛtya devīṃ gāndhārīṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca pārthivam provāca duḥkhaśokārtaḥ kṣatradharmaṃ vigarhayan
english: As Duḥśalā spoke thus piteously, Dhanaṃjaya, remembering the lady Gāndhārī and king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, stricken with grief and sorrow, spoke, reviling the warrior's code.

sanskrit: dhik taṃ duryodhanaṃ kṣudraṃ rājyalubdhaṃ ca māninam yatkṛte bāndhavāḥ sarve mayā nītā yamakṣayam
english: "Cursed be that base Duryodhana, greedy for the kingdom and full of pride, for whose sake all our kinsmen were brought by me to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: ity uktvā bahu sāntvādi prasādam akaroj jayaḥ pariṣvajya ca tāṃ prīto visasarja gṛhān prati
english: Having spoken thus and uttered many soothing words, the Victor showed his grace; and embracing her with affection, he sent her back to her home.

sanskrit: duḥśalā cāpi tān yodhān nivārya mahato raṇāt saṃpūjya pārthaṃ prayayau gṛhān prati śubhānanā
english: And Duḥśalā too, of fair face, having held back those warriors from the great battle and honored Pārtha, set out toward her home.

sanskrit: tataḥ saindhavakān yodhān vinirjitya nararṣabhaḥ punar evānvadhāvat sa taṃ hayaṃ kāmacāriṇam
english: Then, having vanquished the warriors of Sindhu, that bull among men once more followed after the horse that roamed at will.

sanskrit: sasāra yajñiyaṃ vīro vidhivat sa viśāṃ pate tārāmṛgam ivākāśe devadevaḥ pinākadhṛk
english: The hero followed the sacrificial horse duly, O lord of peoples, as the God of gods, bearer of the Pināka, follows the deer-star across the sky.

sanskrit: sa ca vājī yatheṣṭena tāṃs tān deśān yathāsukham vicacāra yathākāmaṃ karma pārthasya vardhayan
english: And that steed, roaming as it pleased through one land after another at its ease and according to its desire, increased the glory of Pārtha's deeds.

sanskrit: krameṇa sa hayas tv evaṃ vicaran bharatarṣabha maṇipūrapater deśam upāyāt sahapāṇḍavaḥ
english: Thus wandering by stages, O bull of the Bhāratas, that horse, accompanied by the Pāṇḍava, came to the realm of the lord of Maṇipūra.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā tu nṛpatir vīraṃ pitaraṃ babhruvāhanaḥ niryayau vinayenāryo brāhmaṇārghyapuraḥsaraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When king Babhruvāhana heard that his heroic father had come, the noble one went forth in humility, with Brāhmaṇas bearing the offering of welcome before him.

sanskrit: maṇipūreśvaraṃ tv evam upayātaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ nābhyanandata medhāvī kṣatradharmam anusmaran
english: But the wise Dhanaṃjaya, mindful of the warrior's code, did not welcome the lord of Maṇipūra who had thus come to meet him.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ dharmātmā samanyuḥ phalgunas tadā prakriyeyaṃ na te yuktā bahis tvaṃ kṣatradharmataḥ
english: And the righteous Phalguna, filled with anger, then said to him: "This conduct of yours is not fitting; you stand outside the duty of a Kṣatriya."

sanskrit: saṃrakṣyamāṇaṃ turagaṃ yaudhiṣṭhiram upāgatam yajñiyaṃ viṣayānte māṃ nāyotsīḥ kiṃ nu putraka
english: "This sacrificial horse of Yudhiṣṭhira, guarded by me, has come to the border of your realm; why then, my son, do you not give me battle?"

sanskrit: dhik tvām astu sudurbuddhiṃ kṣatradharmāviśāradam yo māṃ yuddhāya saṃprāptaṃ sāmnaivātho tvam agrahīḥ
english: "Shame upon you, dull-witted and unskilled in the warrior's code, who, when I have come for battle, would receive me with mere words of peace!"

sanskrit: na tvayā puruṣārthaś ca kaś cid astīha jīvatā yas tvaṃ strīvad yudhā prāptaṃ sāmnā māṃ pratyagṛhṇathāḥ
english: "No purpose of manhood is served by your living here, you who, like a woman, would meet me with conciliation when I have come arrayed for battle."

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ nyastaśastras tvām āgaccheyaṃ sudurmate prakriyeyaṃ tato yuktā bhavet tava narādhama
english: "Had I come to you with weapons laid aside, O most foolish one, then this conduct of yours would be fitting, O basest of men."

sanskrit: tam evam uktaṃ bhartrā tu viditvā pannagātmajā amṛṣyamāṇā bhittvorvīm ulūpī tam upāgamat
english: When the serpent's daughter Ulūpī learned that he had been thus addressed by her husband, unable to bear it, she split the earth and came up to him.

sanskrit: sā dadarśa tataḥ putraṃ vimṛśantam adhomukham saṃtarjyamānam asakṛd bhartrā yuddhārthinā vibho
english: She then beheld her son, brooding with downcast face, rebuked again and again by her husband who sought combat, O lord.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā cārusarvāṅgī tam upetyoragātmajā ulūpī prāha vacanaṃ kṣatradharmaviśāradā
english: Then Ulūpī, the serpent's daughter, fair in every limb and skilled in the warrior's code, approached him and spoke these words:

sanskrit: ulūpīṃ māṃ nibodha tvaṃ mātaraṃ pannagātmajām kuruṣva vacanaṃ putra dharmas te bhavitā paraḥ
english: "Know me to be Ulūpī, your mother, daughter of the serpents. Do as I say, my son, and yours shall be the highest dharma."

sanskrit: yudhyasvainaṃ kuruśreṣṭhaṃ dhanaṃjayam ariṃdama evam eṣa hi te prīto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Fight with this Dhanaṃjaya, best of the Kurus, O subduer of foes; for thus, beyond doubt, will he be pleased with you."

sanskrit: evam uddharṣito mātrā sa rājā babhruvāhanaḥ manaś cakre mahātejā yuddhāya bharatarṣabha
english: Thus roused by his mother, that king Babhruvāhana of great splendor set his mind upon battle, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: saṃnahya kāñcanaṃ varma śirastrāṇaṃ ca bhānumat tūṇīraśatasaṃbādham āruroha mahāratham
english: Donning golden armor and a radiant helmet, crowded about with a hundred quivers, he mounted his great chariot.

sanskrit: sarvopakaraṇair yuktaṃ yuktam aśvair manojavaiḥ sucakropaskaraṃ dhīmān hemabhāṇḍapariṣkṛtam
english: The wise one mounted that chariot furnished with every appurtenance, yoked with horses swift as thought, with fine wheels and fittings, adorned with golden trappings.

sanskrit: paramārcitam ucchritya dhvajaṃ siṃhaṃ hiraṇmayam prayayau pārtham uddiśya sa rājā babhruvāhanaḥ
english: Raising aloft his highly honored banner bearing a golden lion, that king Babhruvāhana set forth against Pārtha.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyetya hayaṃ vīro yajñiyaṃ pārtharakṣitam grāhayām āsa puruṣair hayaśikṣāviśāradaiḥ
english: Then the hero, approaching the sacrificial horse guarded by Pārtha, had it seized by men skilled in the handling of horses.

sanskrit: gṛhītaṃ vājinaṃ dṛṣṭvā prītātmā sa dhanaṃjayaḥ putraṃ rathasthaṃ bhūmiṣṭhaḥ saṃnyavārayad āhave
english: Seeing the steed seized, Dhanaṃjaya was glad at heart; and standing on the ground, he confronted his son, who stood in his chariot, in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā taṃ vīraṃ śaravrātaiḥ sahasraśaḥ ardayām āsa niśitair āśīviṣaviṣopamaiḥ
english: Then that king tormented the hero with showers of arrows by the thousand, keen and like the venom of serpents.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ pituḥ putrasya cātulam devāsuraraṇaprakhyam ubhayoḥ prīyamāṇayoḥ
english: A matchless battle arose between the two, father and son, like the war of gods and Asuras, both of them delighting in it.

sanskrit: kirīṭinaṃ tu vivyādha śareṇa nataparvaṇā jatrudeśe naravyāghraḥ prahasan babhruvāhanaḥ
english: With a smile, the tiger among men Babhruvāhana pierced the Diademed One with a smooth-jointed arrow in the region of the collarbone.

sanskrit: so 'bhyagāt saha puṅkhena valmīkam iva pannagaḥ vinirbhidya ca kaunteyaṃ mahītalam athāviśat
english: The arrow, feathered shaft and all, sank in as a serpent enters an anthill; and piercing through the son of Kuntī, it entered the earth.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhavedano dhīmān ālambya dhanur uttamam divyaṃ tejaḥ samāviśya pramīta iva saṃbabhau
english: Sorely pained, the wise one, leaning upon his excellent bow, gathered up his divine energy and stood as though lifeless to behold.

sanskrit: sa saṃjñām upalabhyātha praśasya puruṣarṣabhaḥ putraṃ śakrātmajo vākyam idam āha mahīpate
english: Then, recovering his senses, that bull among men, the son of Śakra, praising his son, spoke these words, O lord of the earth:

sanskrit: sādhu sādhu mahābāho vatsa citrāṅgadātmaja sadṛśaṃ karma te dṛṣṭvā prītimān asmi putraka
english: "Well done, well done, O mighty-armed son of Citrāṅgadā! Seeing this deed worthy of your lineage, I am pleased with you, my child."

sanskrit: vimuñcāmy eṣa bāṇāṃs te putra yuddhe sthiro bhava ity evam uktvā nārācair abhyavarṣad amitrahā
english: "I now loose my arrows upon you, my son; stand firm in the fight!" So saying, the slayer of foes rained down iron shafts upon him.

sanskrit: tān sa gāṇḍīvanirmuktān vajrāśanisamaprabhān nārācair acchinad rājā sarvān eva tridhā tridhā
english: Those shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, bright as thunderbolt and lightning, the king cut every one of them with his own iron arrows, each into three.

sanskrit: tasya pārthaḥ śarair divyair dhvajaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam suvarṇatālapratimaṃ kṣureṇāpāharad rathāt
english: With his divine arrows Pārtha struck down from his chariot his banner, adorned with gold and shaped like a golden palmyra, with a razor-edged shaft.

sanskrit: hayāṃś cāsya mahākāyān mahāvegaparākramān cakāra rājño nirjīvān prahasan pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ
english: And the bull of the Pāṇḍavas, with a smile, slew the king's horses, huge of body and of great speed and might, leaving them lifeless.

sanskrit: sa rathād avatīryāśu rājā paramakopanaḥ padātiḥ pitaraṃ kopād yodhayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: Swiftly descending from his chariot, the king in utmost fury fought his father the Pāṇḍava on foot, out of wrath.

sanskrit: saṃprīyamāṇaḥ pāṇḍūnām ṛṣabhaḥ putravikramāt nātyarthaṃ pīḍayām āsa putraṃ vajradharātmajaḥ
english: Greatly delighted at his son's valor, the bull of the Pāṇḍavas, the son of the wielder of the thunderbolt, did not press his son too hard.

sanskrit: sa hanyamāno vimukhaṃ pitaraṃ babhruvāhanaḥ śarair āśīviṣākāraiḥ punar evārdayad balī
english: Though hard pressed, the mighty Babhruvāhana, finding his father turned aside, once more tormented him with arrows shaped like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bālyāt pitaraṃ vivyādha hṛdi patriṇā niśitena supuṅkhena balavad babhruvāhanaḥ
english: Then, out of boyish impetuosity, the mighty Babhruvāhana pierced his father in the breast with a keen, well-feathered, winged shaft.

sanskrit: sa bāṇas tejasā dīpto jvalann iva hutāśanaḥ viveśa pāṇḍavaṃ rājan marma bhittvātiduḥkhakṛt
english: That arrow, blazing with energy like flaming fire, entered the Pāṇḍava, O king, piercing a vital part and causing terrible pain.

sanskrit: sa tenātibhṛśaṃ viddhaḥ putreṇa kurunandanaḥ mahīṃ jagāma mohārtas tato rājan dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Thus most grievously wounded by his son, the joy of the Kurus, Dhanaṃjaya, overcome by a swoon, then sank to the earth, O king.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre kauravāṇāṃ dhuraṃdhare so 'pi mohaṃ jagāmāśu tataś citrāṅgadāsutaḥ
english: When that hero, the foremost bearer of the Kaurava burden, had fallen, the son of Citrāṅgadā too at once swooned away.

sanskrit: vyāyamya saṃyuge rājā dṛṣṭvā ca pitaraṃ hatam pūrvam eva ca bāṇaughair gāḍhaviddho 'rjunena saḥ
english: Worn out by his exertions in the fight, and seeing his father slain, and himself sorely wounded before by Arjuna's floods of arrows, that king swooned.

sanskrit: bhartāraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā putraṃ ca patitaṃ bhuvi citrāṅgadā paritrastā praviveśa raṇājiram
english: Seeing her husband slain and her son fallen upon the ground, Citrāṅgadā, stricken with terror, entered the field of battle.

sanskrit: śokasaṃtaptahṛdayā rudatī sā tataḥ śubhā maṇipūrapater mātā dadarśa nihataṃ patim
english: Her heart consumed with grief, weeping, the fair mother of the lord of Maṇipūra then beheld her slain husband.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato bahuvidhaṃ bhīrur vilapya kamalekṣaṇā mumoha duḥkhād durdharṣā nipapāta ca bhūtale
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the timid, lotus-eyed lady, lamenting in many ways, swooned from grief; unassailable as she was, she fell upon the ground.

sanskrit: pratilabhya ca sā saṃjñāṃ devī divyavapurdharā ulūpīṃ pannagasutāṃ dṛṣṭvedaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: And regaining her senses, that lady of divine form, beholding Ulūpī the serpent's daughter, spoke these words:

sanskrit: ulūpi paśya bhartāraṃ śayānaṃ nihataṃ raṇe tvatkṛte mama putreṇa bālena samitiṃjayam
english: "Ulūpī, behold my husband, the victor in battle, lying slain in the field — slain for your sake by my son, a mere boy!"

sanskrit: nanu tvam ārye dharmajñā nanu cāsi pativratā yat tvatkṛte 'yaṃ patitaḥ patis te nihato raṇe
english: "Are you not, O noble one, a knower of dharma, and devoted to your husband? Yet for your sake this lord has fallen, your husband slain in battle."

sanskrit: kiṃ tu sarvāparādho 'yaṃ yadi te 'dya dhanaṃjayaḥ kṣamasva yācyamānā me saṃjīvaya dhanaṃjayam
english: "But if Dhanaṃjaya has wholly wronged you this day — forgive him, I beseech you; bring Dhanaṃjaya back to life!"

sanskrit: nanu tvam ārye dharmajñā trailokyaviditā śubhe yad ghātayitvā bhartāraṃ putreṇeha na śocasi
english: "Are you not, O noble and fair one, a knower of dharma, renowned through the three worlds — that, having caused your husband to be slain here by my son, you do not grieve?"

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śocāmi tanayaṃ nihataṃ pannagātmaje patim eva tu śocāmi yasyātithyam idaṃ kṛtam
english: "I do not grieve for my slain son, O daughter of the serpents; it is my husband alone I grieve for, to whom this hospitality has been shown."

sanskrit: ity uktvā sā tadā devīm ulūpīṃ pannagātmajām bhartāram abhigamyedam ity uvāca yaśasvinī
english: Having so spoken to the lady Ulūpī, the serpent's daughter, the illustrious one then went up to her husband and said this:

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha kurumukhyasya priyakāma mama priya ayam aśvo mahābāho mayā te parimokṣitaḥ
english: "Arise, O beloved, you who would do the will of the chief of the Kurus! O mighty-armed one, this horse of yours has been released by me."

sanskrit: nanu nāma tvayā vīra dharmarājasya yajñiyaḥ ayam aśvo 'nusartavyaḥ sa śeṣe kiṃ mahītale
english: "Surely, O hero, this sacrificial horse of the King of Dharma was to be followed by you; why then do you lie upon the bare earth?"

sanskrit: tvayi prāṇāḥ samāyattāḥ kurūṇāṃ kurunandana sa kasmāt prāṇado 'nyeṣāṃ prāṇān saṃtyaktavān asi
english: "Upon you, O joy of the Kurus, depend the lives of the Kurus; why then have you, the giver of life to others, yourself given up your life?"

sanskrit: ulūpi sādhu saṃpaśya bhartāraṃ nihataṃ raṇe putraṃ cainaṃ samutsāhya ghātayitvā na śocasi
english: "Ulūpī, look well upon my husband slain in battle! Having spurred on this boy, my son, and caused him to slay his father, do you not grieve?"

sanskrit: kāmaṃ svapitu bālo 'yaṃ bhūmau pretagatiṃ gataḥ lohitākṣo guḍākeśo vijayaḥ sādhu jīvatu
english: "Let this boy sleep on, if he must, gone to the path of the dead upon the ground; but let the red-eyed, thick-haired Vijaya live again — that is well."

sanskrit: nāparādho 'sti subhage narāṇāṃ bahubhāryatā nārīṇāṃ tu bhavaty etan mā te bhūd buddhir īdṛśī
english: "It is no fault in men, O fair one, to have many wives; but for women this would be a fault. Let no such thought be yours."

sanskrit: sakhyaṃ hy etat kṛtaṃ dhātrā śāśvataṃ cāvyayaṃ ca ha sakhyaṃ samabhijānīhi satyaṃ saṃgatam astu te
english: "This friendship between us was made by the Creator, eternal and imperishable. Acknowledge this friendship; let our union be true and abiding for you."

sanskrit: putreṇa ghātayitvemaṃ patiṃ yadi na me 'dya vai jīvantaṃ darśayasy adya parityakṣyāmi jīvitam
english: "If, having caused this husband of mine to be slain by my son, you do not show him to me alive this very day, I will give up my life."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ duḥkhānvitā bhīru patiputravinākṛtā ihaiva prāyam āśiṣye prekṣantyās te na saṃśayaḥ
english: "I, O timid one, overwhelmed with grief, bereft of husband and son, will here and now sit fasting unto death before your very eyes, beyond all doubt."

sanskrit: ity uktvā pannagasutāṃ sapatnīṃ caitravāhinī tataḥ prāyam upāsīnā tūṣṇīm āsīj janādhipa
english: Having so spoken to her co-wife, the serpent's daughter, Caitravāhinī then sat down to fast unto death and fell silent, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā vilapyoparatā bhartuḥ pādau pragṛhya sā upaviṣṭābhavad devī socchvāsaṃ putram īkṣatī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having lamented thus and fallen silent, the lady, clasping her husband's feet, sat down, gazing at her son who still drew breath.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃjñāṃ punar labdhvā sa rājā babhruvāhanaḥ mātaraṃ tām athālokya raṇabhūmāv athābravīt
english: Then, regaining his senses, that king Babhruvāhana, looking upon his mother there on the field of battle, spoke:

sanskrit: ito duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu yan me mātā sukhaidhitā bhūmau nipatitaṃ vīram anuśete mṛtaṃ patim
english: "What can be more grievous than this, that my mother, reared in comfort, lies upon the earth beside her fallen hero, her dead husband?"

sanskrit: nihantāraṃ raṇe 'rīṇāṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam mayā vinihataṃ saṃkhye prekṣate durmaraṃ bata
english: "She gazes upon him, the slayer of foes in battle, the best of all bearers of arms, struck down by me in combat. Hard indeed it is to die!"

sanskrit: aho 'syā hṛdayaṃ devyā dṛḍhaṃ yan na vidīryate vyūḍhoraskaṃ mahābāhuṃ prekṣantyā nihataṃ patim
english: "Ah, how firm is this lady's heart, that it does not break asunder as she gazes upon her slain husband, broad-chested and mighty-armed!"

sanskrit: durmaraṃ puruṣeṇeha manye hy adhvany anāgate yatra nāhaṃ na me mātā viprayujyeta jīvitāt
english: "Hard, I think, is it for a man to die before his appointed hour has come — since neither I nor my mother is parted from life."

sanskrit: aho dhik kuruvīrasya hy uraḥsthaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhuvi vyapaviddhaṃ hatasyeha mayā putreṇa paśyata
english: "Alas, look! The golden ornament from the breast of the Kuru hero, slain here by me his son, lies cast away upon the ground."

sanskrit: bho bho paśyata me vīraṃ pitaraṃ brāhmaṇā bhuvi śayānaṃ vīraśayane mayā putreṇa pātitam
english: "Ho, Brāhmaṇas, behold my heroic father lying upon the earth, upon the hero's bed, struck down by me his son!"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kurumukhyasya prayuktā hayasāriṇaḥ kurvantu śāntikāṃ tv adya raṇe yo 'yaṃ mayā hataḥ
english: "Let the Brāhmaṇas appointed as keepers of the horse for the chief of the Kurus now perform the rite of expiation for him whom I have slain this day in battle."

sanskrit: vyādiśantu ca kiṃ viprāḥ prāyaścittam ihādya me sunṛśaṃsasya pāpasya pitṛhantū raṇājire
english: "And let the Brāhmaṇas prescribe what penance is now to be mine — cruel and sinful as I am, the slayer of my own father on the field of battle."

sanskrit: duścarā dvādaśa samā hatvā pitaram adya vai mameha sunṛśaṃsasya saṃvītasyāsya carmaṇā
english: "For me, most cruel one, having this day slain my father, a hard penance of twelve years, clad in this hide,"

sanskrit: śiraḥkapāle cāsyaiva bhuñjataḥ pitur adya me prāyaścittaṃ hi nāsty anyad dhatvādya pitaraṃ mama
english: "and eating from the very skull of this my father — no other expiation is there for me, having slain my father this day."

sanskrit: paśya nāgottamasute bhartāraṃ nihataṃ mayā kṛtaṃ priyaṃ mayā te 'dya nihatya samare 'rjunam
english: "Behold, O daughter of the foremost of serpents, your husband slain by me! A pleasing thing have I done for you this day, by slaying Arjuna in battle."
